To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the population inversion in optical quantum amplifier is accumulated during the time when the pump pulse is present, and the population inversion is not accumulated during the time of pump pulse absence.

the population inversion in the amplifier can be described by the phenomenological model, which takes into account the pumping and the gain, that the population inversion can reach the steady-state value in a short time (about 100 ns), and that the energy utilization efficiency can be optimized by using the net efficiency.

the development of a phenomenological model describing the dynamics of accumulation of population inversion in optical quantum amplifier subjected to pulsed excitation and with the application of the results of this model to the analysis of the operation of high-energy systems of this type.
